newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse industrial head outlines goals.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse industrial head outlines goals.

text.p: The newly appointed chief executive of Westinghouse Electric Corp's industrial group aims to boost margins and shareholder value by streamlining processes and marketing new technologies around the world.

"We're going to have to get better margins and focus on creating additional shareholder value," Ernest H. Drew told Reuters in a telephone interview on Friday. "My goal would be to double the market value of the company."

Earlier, Westinghouse said Drew would become president and chief executive of its Industries and Technology Group, a newly created position, effective July 1. He was also designated as president and CEO of Westinghouse Electric Co, the Pittsburgh-based industrial company that will be formed when Westinghouse splits its media and industrial operations into separate companies in September.
Drew currently is a member of the eight-person senior executive management team at German chemicals producer Hoechst AG.
Wall Street analysts for several months had speculated that Westinghouse Chairman Michael Jordan would tap an outside management talent to run the industrial company.

Drew, 60, said streamlining supply and distribution processes and making them more efficient with new technology often translates into higher margins, and he plans to examine those processes when he arrives at Westinghouse.

"(Streamlining) doesn't necessarily mean (reducing) head count," he said. "Some of these systems were set up before we had the technical capabilities we have now. I certainly will be looking at that."

Drew said Westinghouse's industrial group -- which consists of Power Generation, Thermo King, Energy Systems and Government and Environmental Operations -- also needed to deliver new technology quickly to global markets in order to stay competitive.
With the exception of Thermo King, a refrigerated transportation unit, the industrial operations have faced sluggish markets and margins in recent years.
In this year's first quarter, the industrial group had an operating loss of $59 million, versus a $1 million loss a year earlier.
Drew said Westinghouse has the opportunity to improve its industrial performance by supplying growing markets, including China, India and the Americas, with power generation and nuclear services.
"The key growth areas are Asia and the Americas, as well as places like India," he said. "Because of utility restructuring, there's a lot going on in those areas and that means growth opportunity."
Hoechst analysts said Drew's management and technical background should put him in a good position at Westinghouse to bring about a turnaround of the industrial group.
